Subject: MAP check-in — acceptance window at risk

Hi Samir / Olivia —

Quick heads up: during today's sync Procurement flagged that the security review for our private deployment (SOC2 evidence) won't complete until the week of May 12. That pushes Helix's acceptance window beyond the MAP target of May 8 and puts the close at risk.

Actions I need from you:
- Can Procurement confirm the blocker (budget vs security artifact) and whether a conditional PO is possible?
- If the security review is the holdup, can you share the specific evidence item(s) they need from the SOC2 pack? We attached our current MAP (MAP_Helix_v1.3.xlsx) and the SOC2 evidence checklist — happy to provide anything missing.

Suggested immediate mitigation (for discussion):
- Short re-baseline: shift acceptance window +2 weeks and add a phased acceptance for core inference APIs so dev can start integration earlier.
- Or: pilot cutover for 50 users + procurement conditional sign-off + escrow for final acceptance.

I know these are sensitive asks — looping Marcus and Mina for possible credit/escrow options and for executive escalation if needed. If you can reply with a clear blocker summary today, we'll prepare a one-page exec note for Helix leadership and our VP Sales.

Thanks —
Grace

--

Hi Grace — thanks for the heads up. Short summary from our side:
- Procurement confirms the primary blocker is the internal security artifact signoff. Our InfoSec team requested a specific SOC2 artifact (control: CC6.2 — evidence of KMS-backed key rotation logs) that wasn't in the pack we reviewed.
- Budget is approved, but legal/procurement will not issue a final PO until InfoSec closes the artifact loop.

Next steps from Helix:
- I can escalate to our InfoSec PM and ask for a target date for the artifact review — earliest realistic slot looks like the week of May 12 given current backlog.
- Procurement would accept a conditional PO if Redwood can provide the KMS log sample and agree to a two-week remediation SLA. We'll need an internal note from Redwood confirming the artifact will be provided and a remediation path if issues appear.

We appreciate the phased acceptance idea — that could help our dev team keep momentum. I'll confirm with Procurement and Sam (InfoSec) and reply by EOD.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Cloud Integrations — Helix Health
samir@helixhealth.com

Thanks Grace — good catch. Two operational pathways we can propose to Helix (we should present both to reduce negotiation cycles):

Option A — Two-week rebaseline + credit
- Move acceptance to May 22 (MAP update).
- Redwood provides a pro-rated service credit (attached: proposed-credit-schedule.pdf) if final acceptance slips beyond the new date.
- InfoSec can be given a KMS log sample under NDA today and we commit to delivering the full audit package within 5 business days after conditional PO.

Option B — Phased delivery (recommended if Helix wants earlier integration)
- Phase 1: Core inference + embeddings available on May 8 for Dev integration (limited throughput).
- Phase 2: Full private deployment acceptance after SOC2 artifact closure by May 22.
- Redwood provides rollback/fallback policy + temporary priority support for the pilot window.

For both options we should:
- Prepare a concise one-page exec note summarizing the ask, proposed credit/escrow terms, and acceptance-test checklist.
- Pre-authorize VP-level escalation (Jordan take note) to prevent delays if Procurement holds after InfoSec signs off.

I attached the proposed-credit-schedule.pdf and a redlined MAP snippet with suggested dates. Grace — can you draft the one-pager and collect the acceptance-test set (we'll review with CS)?

Marcus
